key_insight: AdamFlow combines Wasserstein gradient flows for global, distribution-based surface alignment with Adam-style adaptive optimization to achieve fast, robust surface registration for medical meshes.
problem_solved: Addresses the efficiency vs. robustness trade-off in surface registration: local point matching is fast but fragile, while global alignment is robust but computationally expensive.
method: Model surface meshes as probability measures (point clouds/mass distributions) and formulate registration as minimizing a Wasserstein/distributional alignment cost.
Use gradient-flow dynamics over the Wasserstein space to evolve one surface toward another, yielding a principled global alignment.
Introduce an Adam-inspired adaptive optimizer (AdamFlow) for the gradient flow to accelerate convergence and improve robustness to noise and initialization.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical, scalable registration tool that is both fast and robust, enabling more reliable anatomical shape analysis and faster preprocessing in medical imaging pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input surfaces → distribution encoding → Wasserstein gradient flow with Adam updates → registered surface
Before/after overlay of meshes (transparent target + colored moving mesh) to show alignment quality
Convergence plot comparing iterations/time for AdamFlow vs. baseline methods (faster convergence, fewer oscillations)
Schematic of optimal transport/Wasserstein flow showing mass movement between surfaces
paper_title: AdamFlow: Adam-based Wasserstein Gradient Flows for Surface Registration in Medical Imaging
paper_authors: Qiang Ma, Qingjie Meng, Xin Hu, Yicheng Wu, Wenjia Bai
